rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn says Aaron feared that leaving the Israelites to follow Moses would split them into fighting factions, after which Moses would blame him.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : خشيت إن فارقتهم واتبعتك أن يصيروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا فتقول : أوقعت الفرق فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron had not preserved Moses’ charge to succeed him well: unite the people, preserve cohesion, and deal gently until Moses returned, especially given their strength and the leaders’ weakness.
rows.anchor: يريد به قوله : {اخلفنى فى قومى وأصلح} فإن الإصلاح ضم النشر وحفظ جماعات الناس والمداراة بهم

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: Al-ʿUyūn glosses the phrase as not considering Moses’ situation or not waiting for his return.
rows.anchor: وفي "العيون" : أي : لم تنظر في أمري أو لم تنتظر قدومي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya says waiting for Moses’ word and obeying him kept Aaron from following him; this was not disobedience.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يعني منعني ترقب قولك وإطاعة أمرك عن اتباعك لا عصيان أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron is excusing himself: excuses include denying the deed, explaining it to remove guilt, or admitting it and resolving not to repeat it; the last is repentance, so every repentance is an excuse but not vice versa.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام من هارون اعتذار والعذر تحرى الإنسان ما يمحو به ذنوبه وذلك ثلاثة أضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron was forbearing and gentle, which explains why the Israelites especially loved him.
rows.anchor: حليما رفيقا ولذا كان بنو إسرائيل أشد حباله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī calls love in people’s hearts the finest of treasures.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أحسن الكنوز محبة القلوب

rows.speaker: سقراط
rows.claim: Socrates says good character brings a pleasant life, safety, and love, while poor character sours life and earns hatred.
rows.anchor: قال سقراط : من أحسن خلقه طابت عيشته ودامت سلامته وتأكدت في النفوس محبته

rows.speaker: بزرجمهر
rows.claim: Buzurjmihr links contentment with comfort and humility with love, adding that forbearance may appear weak in some settings but brings glory in others.
rows.anchor: قال بزرجمهر ثمرة القناعة الراحة وثمرة التواضع المحبة

rows.speaker: أرسطو
rows.claim: Aristotle says eloquence raises rank, humility wins love, forbearance gains supporters, gentleness wins hearts, and fidelity sustains brotherhood.
rows.anchor: قال أرسطو بإصابة المنطق يعظم القدر وبالتواضع تكثر المحبة وبالحلم تكثر الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet remained gentle and kind, matching his description as compassionate and merciful toward believers.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي عليه السلام لم يخرج عن حد اللين والرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Mathnawī portraying God’s servants as merciful and patient, bearing divine qualities while gently helping in reform.
rows.anchor: بندكان حق رحيم وبردبار خوى حق دارند در اصلاح كارمهربان بى رشوتان يارى كران

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some define extending the gaze as lingering in admiration and wishing to possess what one sees.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم مد النظر تطويله وأن لا يكاد يرده استحسانا للمنظور إليه وإعجابا به وتمنيا أن له مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A brief glance followed by lowering the eyes is excused as unavoidable; the prohibition targets prolonged admiration, a common human impulse toward finery.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن النظر الغير الممدود معفو عنه لأنه لا يمكن الاحتراز منه

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī transmits from Abū Rāfiʿ that, after a guest arrived and the Prophet lacked provisions, he sought flour on credit from a Jew and pledged his armor; the verse consoled him.
rows.anchor: أبو رافع رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of matāʿ conveys extension and elevation; it can mean useful household goods or enjoyment extended over time.
rows.anchor: وأصل المتوع الامتداد والارتفاع يقال متع النهار ومتع النبات ارتفع

rows.speaker: الكبير
rows.claim: Al-Kabīr glosses mattaʿnā as delighting people through beautiful sights, stirring sounds, pleasant scents, clothing, and marriage.
rows.anchor: وفي "الكبير" : ألذذنا به والامتاع الإلذاذ بما يدرك من المناظر الحسنة ويسمع من الأصوات المطربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The groups enjoying these things are kinds of unbelievers, including polytheists and scripturalists such as Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: أي : أصنافا من الكفرة كالوثنى والكتابي من اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrata is accusative under an understood verb indicated by mattaʿnā: God gave them worldly adornment, splendor, freshness, and beauty.
rows.anchor: منصوب بفعل يدل عليه متعنا أي : أعطينا زينة الدنيا وبهجتها ونضارتها وحسنها

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the verse as consolation for the poor: even the best of creation was barred from admiring worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : هذه تسلية للفقراء وتعزية لهم حيث منع خير الخلق عن النظر إلى الدنيا على وجه الاستحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people through what He gives; some respond to increased favors with greater disbelief and transgression and thus earn punishment.
rows.anchor: أي : لنعاملهم فيما أعطينا معاملة من نبتليهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says not to admire the garments and mounts of the unjust, but to look for sin’s humiliation showing through their finery.
rows.anchor: حتى قال الحسن لا تنظروا إلى دقدقة هماليج الفسقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oppressors acquire displays to attract spectators, so admiring them serves their purpose and encourages further display.
rows.anchor: لأنهم اتخذوا هذه الأشياء لعيون النظارة فالناظر إليها محصل لغرضهم ومغر لهم على اتخاذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls worldly life sweet, green, and beautiful to the eye; the commentary says green evokes freshness and its quick disappearance like vegetation.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن الدنيا" أي : صورتها ومتاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Khujandī’s poem comparing worldly pleasures to honey whose bitterness and trouble exceed its sweetness.
rows.anchor: جهان وجمله لذاتش بزنبور عسل ماند كه شيرينيش بسيارست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawī says that once a person sees through worldly life, it appears like carrion.
rows.anchor: هركه از ديدار بر خوردار شد اين جهان درشم او مردار شد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ portrays the world as a crafty old woman who cloaks seduction in religion, deceives, and departs.
rows.anchor: ازره مرو بعشوه ديني كه اين عجوز مكاره مى نشيند ومحتاله مى رود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ depicts the world as outwardly a beautiful bride whose suitor pays for marriage with his life.
rows.anchor: خوش عروسيست جهان ازره صورت ليكن هركه يوست بدو عمر خودش كابين داد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says God makes people successors in worldly life and watches how they act; their wealth is entrusted property over which they serve as agents.
rows.anchor: أي : جاعلكم خلفاء في الدنيا يعني أن أموالكم ليست هي في الحقيقة لكم

rows.speaker: عيسى بن مريم
rows.claim: Jesus warns people not to make worldly life their lord, lest it make them its slaves.
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لا تتخذوا الدنيا ربا فتتخذكم لها عبيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author follows al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya in reading the two eyes as bodily sight and inner vision, with divine vision admitting no association.
rows.anchor: أي عيني البصر والبصيرة وهما عين الرأس وعين القلب

words: إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًۭا مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Najmī reading extends the allusion to both worldly and afterlife enjoyments, calling for cleansing outer and inner sight of attachment to either.
rows.anchor: اغسل عيني ظاهرك وباطنك بماء العزة عن وصمة رؤية الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, enjoyment of either abode can distract people from attaining the perfection of beholding divine beauty.
rows.anchor: وإنما متعنا أهل الدارين بهما عزة لحضرة جلالنا

rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: When al-Shiblī heard the verse about Paradise’s people being occupied, he gasped that they did not know whose presence occupied them.
rows.anchor: قيل : قرىء عند الشبلي قدس سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s provision may mean afterlife reward stored for him or modest sufficiency received with obedience.
rows.anchor: أي : ما ادخر لك في الآخرة من الثواب أو ما أوتيته من يسير الكفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq can mean a worldly or otherworldly gift, an allotted share, or food that reaches and nourishes the body.
rows.anchor: والرزق يقال للعطاء دنيويا كان أو أخرويا وللنصيب تارة ولما يوصل إلى الجوف ويتغذى به تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision is better because it is the highest object of competition and is safe from worldly harm.
rows.anchor: لأنه مع كونه في نفسه أجل ما يتنافس فيه المتنافسون مأمون الغائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is more enduring because it will not end.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يكاد ينقطع أبدا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī cites Kashf al-Asrār: zahrah means flower; the dinar is called a flower because its freshness lasts only briefly before withering.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در كشف الاسرار آورده كه زهر درلغت شكوفه است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Saʿdī praising contentment with little: worldly sweetness is not worth its sting, and appetite degrades those who indulge it.
rows.anchor: كر آزاده برزمين خسب وبس مكن بهرفانى زمين بوس كس نيرزد عسل جان من زخم نيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most valuable provision nourishes the holy spirit with knowledge, wisdom, primordial effusion, and divine manifestation.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الرزق المعتبر غاية الاعتبار ما صار غذاء للروح القدسي من العلم والحكمة والفيض الأزلي والتجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawī contrasts bread with wisdom and says spiritual nourishment opens the inner mouth to mysteries.
rows.anchor: فهم نان كردى نه حكمت اى رهى زانكه حق كفت كلوا من رزقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor should use prayer to face poverty rather than worry over livelihood or look toward the wealthy.
rows.anchor: يعني : كما أمرناك بالصلاة فأمر أنت أهل بيتك فإن الفقير ينبغي أن يستعين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet used to visit Fāṭima and ʿAlī each morning for months and call them to prayer.
rows.anchor: فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذهب إلى فاطمة وعلي كل صباح

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: ʿArāʾis al-Baqli identifies istibār as the station of struggle and patience as the station of witnessing.
rows.anchor: قال في "عرائس البقلى" : الاصطبار مقام المجاهدة والصبر مقام المشاهدة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ calls istibār the hardest patience: the heart and inner self remain still under trials, while ordinary patience is of the lower self.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء أشد أنواع الصبر الاصطبار وهو السكون تحت موارد البلاء بالسر والقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; He asks him to worship.
rows.anchor: أي : لا نكلفك أن ترزق نفسك ولا أهلك إنما نسألك العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides for the Prophet and his family, freeing his attention for the afterlife; those serving God receive His care.
rows.anchor: وإياهم ففرغ بالك لأمر الآخرة فإن من كان في عمل الله كان الله في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unqualified, al-ʿāqibah denotes the praiseworthy final reward, Paradise.
rows.anchor: الحميدة وهي الجنة فإن إطلاقها يختص بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good end belongs to the God-fearing, meaning the Prophet and his followers; taqwā restrains soul and limbs from what knowledge condemns.
rows.anchor: وهو ذم النفس والجوارح عن جميع ما يقبحه العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hardship struck his household, the Prophet commanded them to pray and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر أمرهم بالصلاة وتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says needs are not sought from God by anything like prayer; earlier believers turned to it in crises and often found relief.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : إن الحوائج لم تطلب من الله تعالى بمثل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jonah was among those who prayed; otherwise he would have remained in the fish until resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني من المصلين للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī draws from the verse that glorification is the most beneficial remedy for an epidemic.
rows.anchor: وعن الشافعي رحمه الله أخذا من هذه الآية لم أر أنفع للوباء من التسبيح

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh pictures prayer and fasting as warp and weft of worshippers’ robes; bodily prayer is obligatory and voluntary prayer, while the soul’s prayer rises toward spiritual nearness.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله للعابدين أردية يكسونها من عند الله سداها الصلاة ولحمتها الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh’s taxonomy, the heart’s prayer is lasting vigilance and presence, and the secret’s prayer is turning from all but God in witnessing.
rows.anchor: وصلاة القلب دوام المراقبة ولزوم المحاضرة كقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit’s prayer is annihilation in God and abiding through God, exemplified by obedience to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الروح فناؤه في الله وبقاؤه بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who attain these forms of prayer are freed from dependence on people and receive God’s provision, as the Prophet’s life illustrates.
rows.anchor: فمن صلى هذه الصلاة أغناه الله عما عند الناس ورزقه مما عنده

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink.
rows.anchor: كان يقول صلى الله عليه وسلم "أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ is Meccan and contains 112 verses.
rows.anchor: مائة واثنتا عشرة آية مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaruba and iqtaraba both mean that something has drawn near.
rows.anchor: يقال قرب الشيء واقترب إذا دنا

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: Al-ʿUyūn says the lām means “from” and attaches to the verb; its phrase is fronted before the subject.
rows.anchor: قال في "العيون" : اللام بمعنى من وهي متعلقة بالفعل وتقديمها على الفاعل

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: Fronting the phrase hastens the frightening news so that the approaching event immediately inspires dread and alarm.
rows.anchor: للمسارعة إلى إدخال الروعة فإن نسبة الاقتراب إليهم من أول الأمر مما يسوؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” means Meccan polytheists who deny resurrection, as the following description of heedlessness and turning away shows.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالناس المشركون المنكرون للبعث من أهل مكة كما يفصح عنه ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥisāb is reckoning: disclosing what is for or against a person so recompense can follow.
rows.anchor: والحساب بمعنى المحاسبة وهو إظهار ما للبعد وما عليه ليجازي على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Resurrection is named the Day of Reckoning after its most consequential event for people’s hearts.
rows.anchor: وسمي يوم القيامة بيوم الحساب تسمية للزمان بأعظم ما وقع فيه وأشده وقعا في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning draws closer after seeming distant: each hour is nearer than the last, though more time has passed than remains.
rows.anchor: فإنه في كل ساعة من ساعات الزمان أقرب إليهم من الساعة السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time is unspecified because concealment is more fitting, as with the time of death.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يعين الوقت لأن كتمانه أصلح كوقت الموت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith compares the remaining time for this community with the interval between afternoon prayer and sunset.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "أما بقاؤكم فيما سلف قبلكم من الأمم كما بين صلاة العصر إلى غروب الشمس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means the time when God accounts for and punishes the Meccan polytheists for evil deeds—the Resurrection—is near.
rows.anchor: والمعنى دنا من مشركي قريش وقت محاسبة الله إياهم على أعمالهم السيئة الموجبة للعقاب

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī quotes a view that reprisal and remembrance of those killed and captured at Badr had drawn near.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي نقلا عن بعض (نزديك شد وقت مؤاخذت وياد داشت ايشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the Badr reprisal reading: death connects immediately to Resurrection, so punishment at death counts as nearing the final reckoning.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا هو الأظهر عندي لأن زمان الموت متصل بزمان القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghफलah is inattention arising from inadequate vigilance and alertness.
rows.anchor: الغفلة سهو يعتري من قلة التحفظ والتيقظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of even the smallest account and unprepared for it, denying its coming rather than merely acknowledging it without concern.
rows.anchor: والحال أنهم في غفلة تامة من الحساب على النقير والقطمير والتأهب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial defies reason: actions require recompense, or obedience and sin would be treated alike against wisdom and justice.
rows.anchor: مع اقتضاء عقولهم لأن الأعمال لا بد لها من الجزاء وإلا لزم التسوية بين المطيع والعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿraḍa means turning away while showing one’s side.
rows.anchor: يقال أعرض أي : ولى مبديا عرضه أي : ناحيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from faith, signs, and warnings that should awaken heedless people.
rows.anchor: عن الإيمان والآيات والنذر المنبهة لهم من سنة الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions of heedlessness and turning away are both predicates of the pronoun.
rows.anchor: وهما خبران للضمير

rows.speaker: حي من خزاعة
rows.claim: A group from Khuzāʿa claimed angels were God’s daughters and that He married leading jinn and fathered angels.
rows.anchor: وقالوا} أي : حي من خزاعة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says akhdh is placing or acquiring a thing, by taking or force, and figuratively applies to fever or a captive.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الأخذ وضع الشيء وتحصيله وذلك تارة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Ittakhadha is the iftiʿāl form of akhdh, takes two objects, and functions like jaʿala.
rows.anchor: والاتخاذ افتعال منه فيتعدى إلى مفعولين ويجري مجرى الجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥānah may be a verbal noun conveying transcendence or remoteness, or a fixed noun for glorification.
rows.anchor: تنزه بالذات تنزهه اللائق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing means “I glorify Him with glorification,” or is an imperative to glorify Him.
rows.anchor: أو أسبحه تسبيحه على أنه علم للتسبيح وهو مقول على ألسنة العباد أو سبحوه تسبيحه

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm allows an exclamation at the foolish claim: how far above child, spouse, and partner is the giver of blessings.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" ويجوز أن يكون تعجبا من كلمتهم الحمقاء أي : ما أبعد من ينعم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says declaring God transcendent does not conflict with expressing astonishment at the claim.
rows.anchor: وقال في "الكشف" التنزيه لا ينافي التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are created and honored servants, preferred over many but not all; createdness rules out offspring because birth implies likeness, while honor does not make them children.
rows.anchor: بل هم {عباد} مخلوقون له تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā is neither preposition nor conjunction here; it begins a clause marking the limit of the prior condition at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: حتى هنا ليس بحرف جر ولا حرف عطف بل حرف يبتدأ بعدها الكلام غاية لما يدل عليه ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yājūj and Mājūj are two human tribes; a report says nine of every ten parts of humanity belong to them.
rows.anchor: ويأجوج ومأجوج قبيلتان من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their opening means the opening of their barrier, with the omitted noun understood; the story of its building and end-time opening appears in Sūrat al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: والمراد بفتحها فتح سدها على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” refers to Yājūj and Mājūj, coming from every elevated part of the earth.
rows.anchor: أي : والحال أن يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib derives ḥadab from a protruding back, then extends the image to raised land and the convex vault of the heavens.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : يجوز أن يكون الأصل في الحدب حدب الظهر وهو خروجه ودخول الصدر والبطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yansilūn means descending swiftly, with quick short strides.
rows.anchor: ينزلون مسرعين وأصله مقاربة الخطو مع الإسراع

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm relates the root to a wolf moving quickly.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" من نسل الذئب إذا أسرع في مشيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they traverse the earth and approach people from every elevated place.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم يسيرون في الأرض ويقبلون على الناس من كل موضع مرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says they overrun the world, drink up its waters, and eat everything they find, dry or moist.
rows.anchor: همه عالم را فرا كيرند وآبهاى درياها تمامى بياشامند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the true promise is coordinated with the clause about the barrier opening.
rows.anchor: عطف على فتحت والمراد ما بعد النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is what follows the second trumpet blast: resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
rows.anchor: والمراد ما بعد النفخة الثانية من البعث والحساب والجزاء

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer uses sudden إذا; “she” is a pronoun of the event, and شاخصة is a fronted predicate of eyes.
rows.anchor: جواب الشرط وإذا للمفاجأة والضمير للقصة وشاخصة خبر مقدم لأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes are fixed open without blinking and raised in terror at the horror of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يقال شخص بصره فهو شاخص إذا فتح عينيه وجعل لا يطرف

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour cannot be delayed after Yājūj and Mājūj emerge; Ḥudhayfa says a person could not ride a foal acquired then before it arrived.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن قيام الساعة لا يتأخر عن خروج يأجوج ومأجوج كما روي عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the barrier opens near the world’s end and fixed gazes occur on Resurrection Day, the short interval between condition and result counts as no interval.
rows.anchor: فالجواب أن التفاوت القليل يجري مجرى العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation is supplied with an implied saying verb and cast as a circumstantial clause: they call woe to come since its time has arrived.
rows.anchor: وهو على تقدير قول وقع حالا من الموصول

words: قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit being wholly heedless in worldly life of resurrection and return to God for recompense.
rows.anchor: تامة في الدنيا والغفلة سهو يعتري من قلة التحفظ والتيقظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their correction rejects mere heedlessness: warned by signs, they were wrongdoers who denied them or exposed themselves to lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: إضراب عما قبله من وصف أنفسهم بالغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should reflect on this reminder: God warned people and removed their excuses.
rows.anchor: فليتفكر العاقل في هذا البيان والتذكار فقد نبه الله وقطع الأعذار

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: God tells jinn and humans that He advised them, their deeds are recorded, and each person should praise Him for good or blame himself otherwise.
rows.anchor: يقول الله يا معشر الجن والإنس إني قد نصحت لكم

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A sage says mourners should pity themselves instead: the dead has escaped seeing the Angel of Death, death agony, and fear of the final end.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الحكماء أنه نظر إلى أناس يترحمون على ميت خلف جنازته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Saʿdī likening the body to a cage and the soul to a bird called breath, urging people to wake from heedlessness while opportunity remains.
rows.anchor: خبر دارى أي : استخواني قفس كه جان تو مرغيست نامش نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿdī warns that time has passed in heedlessness and urges the listener to count a moment as an opportunity.
rows.anchor: جو مارا بغفلت بشد روزكار توبارى دمى ند فرصت شمار

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strive day and night to purify the soul and subdue denial: this greater struggle faces the inward enemy that is hardest to evade.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل الاجتهاد في الليل والنهار لتزكية النفس وقمع الإنكار فإنه جهاد أكبر

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author asks God to protect from enemies and make people follow the clear truth from which there is no deviation.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه أن يحفظنا من شر الأعداء ويجعلنا تابعين للحق الصريح الذي لا محيد عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the people of Mecca who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: يا أهل مكة المنكرين للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿth means bringing people out of the earth and conveying them to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: البعث الإخراج من الأرض والتسيير إلى الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إن appears despite many doubters because the evidence here uproots doubt and frames it as merely hypothetical.
rows.anchor: وجيء بأن مع كثرة المرتابين لاشتمال المقام على ما يقلع الريب من أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubt concerns either whether restoration is possible and within God’s power, or whether resurrection will occur.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم في شك من إمكان الإعادة وكونها مقدورة له تعالى أو من وقوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation clause is not the conditional answer, since creation preceded doubt; it is evidence for an omitted answer: consider your origin and doubt will disappear.
rows.anchor: ليس جزاء للشرط لأن خلقهم مقدم على كونهم مرتابين بل هو علة للجزاء المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was first created collectively from dust through Adam.
rows.anchor: فرد منكم خلقا إجماليا {من تراب}

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says God made the earth tractable beneath people and created humans from dust to humble them; they instead chose arrogance, and pride bars entry to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن الله جعل الأرض ذلولا تمشون في مناكبها وخلق بني آدم من تراب ليذلهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfah is clear water, little or much, and by extension male semen; the name derives from water flowing or being poured.
rows.anchor: هي الماء الصافي قل أو كثر ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqah is a clotted piece of blood formed from semen.
rows.anchor: قطعة من الدم جامدة مكونة من المني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍghah is a piece of flesh formed from clot, originally the amount that can be chewed.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة من اللحم مكونة من العلق وهي في الأصل مقدار ما يمضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhallaqah is genitive as an adjective modifying muḍghah.
rows.anchor: بالجر صفة مضغة أي مستبينة الخلق مصورة

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says an unformed morsel has no distinct shape yet: first no limbs are visible, then some appear; the last state is “unformed” as a privation.
rows.anchor: لم يستبن خلقها وصورتها بعد والمراد تفصيل حال المضغة

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The Najmī inward reading calls the formed morsel one into which the spirit has been breathed and the unformed one an image without a soul.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قول حضرة النجم في "التأويلات" : {مخلقة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says each person’s creation is gathered in the mother’s womb for forty days; gathering is securing the material of creation, and “womb” names the whole for a part.
rows.anchor: أي : يحرز ويقر مادة خلقه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the drop spreads beneath the woman’s skin, nails, and hair, stays forty nights, descends as blood, then becomes a clot and morsel for equivalent periods before the spirit is breathed in.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن النطفة إذا وقعت في الرحم فأراد الله أن يخلق منها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In Ibn Masʿūd’s report, an angel is sent to write provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether the person is destined for misery or happiness.
rows.anchor: يعني يؤمر الملك بكتابة أربع من القضايا وكل قضية سميت كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report suggests image formation in the second forty days, but the author says this means it is then decreed, since visible formation normally follows the morsel stage.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن التصوير يكون في الأربعين الثاني لكن المراد تقدير تصويرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miserable person is destined for the Fire and the happy person for Paradise; misery is mentioned first because most people fall into that class.
rows.anchor: وهو من وجبت له النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people through these remarkable stages to clarify resurrection: whoever first created humans from lifeless dust can restore them.
rows.anchor: أي خلقناكم على هذا النمط البديع لنبين لكم بذلك أمر البعث والنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited couplets make the same inference: the One able to create people initially has manifest power to resurrect them.
rows.anchor: بعث إنسان كرنشد عيان أول خلقش هذا بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins a new clause describing what God wills to keep in the womb after creation, until a set term.
rows.anchor: استئناف مسوق لبيان حالهم بعد تمام خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term is delivery; its minimum is six months by agreement, while jurists differ on its maximum.
rows.anchor: وقت معين هو وقت الوضع وأدناه ستة أشهر عند الكل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa sets the maximum pregnancy term at two years.
rows.anchor: وأقصاه سنتان عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī sets the maximum pregnancy term at four years.
rows.anchor: وأربع سنين عند الشافعي

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik sets the maximum pregnancy term at five years.
rows.anchor: وخمس سنين عند مالك

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: The Successor al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim is reported to have remained in the womb for two years.
rows.anchor: روي : أن الضحاك بن مزاحم التابعي مكث في بطن أمه سنتين

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik is reported to have remained in the womb three years; al-Suyūṭī mentions this alongside the report about al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: ومالكا ثلاث سنين كما ذكره السيوطي

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imām reports that a neighbor bore three children in twelve years, with four years of pregnancy each time.
rows.anchor: وأخبر الإمام رحمه الله أن جارة له ولدت ثلاثة أولاد في اثنتي عشرة سنة تحمل أربع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some pregnancies are not retained after development is complete and end in miscarriage.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن بعض ما في الأرحام لا يشاء الله تعالى إقراره فيها بعد تكامل خلقه فيسقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end of the fixed term, God brings people out from their mothers’ wombs.
rows.anchor: أي من بطون أمهاتكم بعد إقراركم فيها عند تمام الأجل المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ṭiflan applies to each child or is a generic form covering one or many.
rows.anchor: والأفراد باعتبار كل واحد منهم أو بإرادة الجنس المنتظم للواحد والمتعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭifl refers to a soft, tender child.
rows.anchor: والطفل الولد ما دام ناعما كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: المولى الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanārī defines the child stage as birth and first cry through the end of six years.
rows.anchor: وقال المولى الفناري في تفسير الفاتحة حد الطفل من أول ما يولد إلى أن يستهل صارخا إلى انقضاء ستة أعوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of reaching maturity is coordinated with the purpose of bringing people out: they grow gradually to adulthood.
rows.anchor: علة لنخرجكم معطوفة على علة أخرى مناسبة لها كأنه قيل ثم نخرجكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching full strength means completeness in power, reason, and discernment, usually between thirty and forty.
rows.anchor: كما لكم في القوة والعقل والتمييز وهو فيما بين الثلاثين والأربعين

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives ashudd as eighteen to thirty years and notes its singular form follows a plural pattern like ānuk.
rows.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين واحد جاء على بناء الجمع كآنك ولا نظير لهما
